reviews.summary: Sacnilk revised overseas receipts for 16–20 November. The five daily changes add ₹24.00 crore to the worldwide run. The dated report agrees with the revised series. US and Canadian receipts still include a provisional $500,000 for Friday.
reviews.next: Recheck the 20 November North American estimate and the 21 November full-day gross. Sacnilk lists ₹33.05 crore in India and ₹53.05 crore worldwide on Saturday. The Numbers stops on Friday, Mojo’s Saturday chart was empty, and Boxoffy’s count was partial.

reviews.summary: Friday 20 November remains the common cutoff. The Numbers and Box Office Mojo list $500,000 for Friday in the US and Canada. Boxoffy estimates about $830,000 for Saturday from 52,448 counted tickets. The new weekend tables show each publisher’s theater count and gross per theater.
reviews.next: Check The Numbers and Box Office Mojo for a full-day US and Canadian gross and cumulative total for 21 November, and for confirmation of Friday’s estimate. Sacnilk reports ₹33.05 crore in India and ₹53.05 crore worldwide on Saturday, taking its cumulative totals to ₹1,084.00 crore and ₹1,651.00 crore.

reviews.summary: Edition 3 adds six weekly market charts, figures for 24 other markets, two release watchlists and reception from five additional markets. Reporting periods vary by market. The daily series retains the reconciled R-002 totals through 20 November.
reviews.next: Check the next international charts as their publishers release them, including the first local grosses for Brazil and Mexico. Revisit the 20 November US/Canada estimate and the full-day 21 November report before extending the daily charts.

reviews.summary: The third weekend added ₹137.35 crore worldwide and ₹94.35 crore in India on Sacnilk’s gross series. The Numbers estimates $2.171 million in the US and Canada. Four revised worldwide entries reduce the earlier 20 November total by ₹15 crore.

sourceNotes.text: The Numbers revised Friday to $494,000. Its three provisional daily entries bring the series to $28,514,872, which rounds to its published $28,515,000. Mojo’s complete daily rows add to $2,065,000 for the weekend and $28,408,872 through Sunday. Its weekend page showed a Friday–Saturday subtotal at review time.

Sacnilk’s revised daily rows sum to the dated Sunday worldwide total of ₹1,689.50 crore. Bollywood Hungama maintains its own India series. Its India net and Sacnilk’s tax-inclusive India gross measure different receipts.

Two additions fill gaps in the existing sources. The Cinetel chart on ComingSoon.it extends Italian coverage beyond opening day. Comscore’s estimates, as reported by Bollywood Hungama, supply a worldwide weekend rank in US dollars across 64 territories.

reviews.next: Recheck US/Canada weekend actuals against the daily and weekend reports. Read the next Dutch and Nigerian film-level charts and the New Zealand local-currency report. Revisit Brazil’s ANCINE data and Mexico’s CANACINE chart for their first verified local grosses.

reviews.summary: Through Monday, Ramayana earned $28,803,257 in the US and Canada. Sacnilk estimates ₹1,141.65 crore gross in India and ₹1,709.65 crore worldwide. The confirmed US/Canada third weekend came to $2,161,159, down $9,841 from the estimate.

sourceNotes.text: The Numbers’ dated Monday chart and its film table report $298,226 for the day, bringing the total to $28,803,257. The film table had initially listed $300,000. Mojo confirms all three weekend days. Its Monday chart had no figure at review time.
Sacnilk’s day-19 worldwide estimate includes ₹568 crore overseas. Monday’s ₹5 crore overseas brings the worldwide total to ₹1,709.65 crore, above the ₹1,704.65 crore in early coverage.
The Tuesday briefing uses Sacnilk’s day-20 report for India and worldwide. All three daily chart series close on Monday.

reviews.next: Check the full Tuesday US/Canada gross and cumulative total against the revised Monday base before adding 24 November to the charts. Revisit the Nigerian and New Zealand weekend charts and the Brazil and Mexico watchlists.

reviews.summary: Monday’s US/Canada gross of $298,226 now appears on both The Numbers and Box Office Mojo, taking the run to $28,803,257. Tuesday brought estimated Indian admissions above 40 million. New weekend reports cover Hungary’s opening and Thailand’s third weekend.

sourceNotes.text: Mojo’s Monday chart places Ramayana ninth and matches The Numbers to the dollar. Its Tuesday chart had no entries at the evening check. Boxoffy’s Tuesday North American seat count was still partial.

Sacnilk’s Tuesday report gives ₹20.50 crore gross in India and ₹25.50 crore worldwide for the day. Through Tuesday, that is ₹1,162.15 crore in India and ₹1,735.15 crore worldwide. Monday is the latest day with comparable grosses in all three markets.

The Hungarian distributors’ opening-weekend chart lists receipts in forints and admissions in tickets. Thailand Box Office gives a nationwide estimate in baht. Several US-dollar territory totals in The Numbers have no stated closing date.

reviews.next: Check the full Tuesday US/Canada gross and running total against $28,803,257 through Monday. Revisit the Nigerian and New Zealand weekend charts and the Brazil and Mexico watchlists.

reviews.summary: The US and Canada passed $30 million on Thanksgiving. Through Thursday, Sacnilk estimates ₹1,185 crore gross in India and ₹1,775 crore worldwide. The map shows 13 openings on November 26 and Iceland’s first reported weekend, $5,373 from two theaters.

sourceNotes.text: The Numbers and Box Office Mojo agree on Tuesday’s $418,368 and Wednesday’s $385,000. The Numbers reports $480,000 for Thursday, when Mojo’s chart had yet to list the film. The two rounded holiday grosses are marked provisional pending final reporting.

Sacnilk raised Tuesday’s overseas estimate from ₹5 crore to ₹8 crore, bringing Tuesday’s worldwide total to ₹1,738.15 crore. Thursday’s dated report and daily ledger agree on ₹590 crore overseas and ₹1,775 crore worldwide. India Today carried ₹592 crore overseas and ₹1,777 crore worldwide. The ₹2 crore difference is entirely overseas.

Friday’s Indian and worldwide figures are evening estimates. The three shared charts close on Thursday, the latest date with a full-day report for the US and Canada. Each local market on the map keeps its own reporting date.

reviews.next: Check final US/Canada receipts for November 25–26 and the first Friday report. Reconcile Friday’s India and worldwide estimates. Look for opening-weekend grosses in Latin America and Czechia.

opportunities.title: North American theater counts
opportunities.next: All three weekend grosses match the daily ledger. For 13–15 November, The Numbers reports 1,110 theaters and Box Office Mojo reports 1,112. Keep both attributions when revisiting these weekends.

opportunities.next: Read the next weekend workbook and its preview footnotes. Preserve the £1 difference between the two publishers in the 13–15 November reports.

opportunities.title: India admissions and language mix
opportunities.next: Check dated reports for two complete periods. Record footfalls and language-level net in separate series, reconciling the language sum to all-India net within rounding.

opportunities.title: Effect of the exchange rate
opportunities.next: Match two reported gross dates to available H.10 observations and document the holiday rule before showing a dated-rate comparison.

items.topic: India passes ₹1,000 crore net in the evening estimate
items.text: At 10:27 p.m. IST, Sacnilk estimated ₹1,000.55 crore net in India and ₹1,195.10 crore gross. Its worldwide estimate of ₹1,790.10 crore would put Ramayana just ₹2.04 crore above Baahubali 2’s lifetime total. That lead depends on Friday’s provisional receipts.

items.topic: Producers report Indian-film records in 27 countries
items.text: The producers named Thailand, Indonesia and the Netherlands among the 27 countries where they say Ramayana set a record for an Indian production. They have yet to release a gross for every country.

items.topic: Taiwan has a December opening date
items.text: Venice Cinemas lists December 11 in Taiwan. India Today reports that mainland China, Japan, South Korea and Russia are being considered for early 2027, subject to scheduling and approvals.

items.topic: Thanksgiving takes the US and Canada past $30 million
items.text: The Numbers reports $480,000 across 405 theaters on Thursday. That brings the run to $30,086,625, up from $29,606,625 on Wednesday.

items.topic: Ramayana opens in more Latin American and European cinemas
items.text: The release map records 13 Thursday openings. They include Chile, where Andes Films distributed the film, Argentina, where Cines Multiplex lists a Spanish-language release, and Czechia, where Cinema City lists the local premiere. Opening grosses for these markets are pending.
Wednesday added an estimated ₹11.35 crore in India and ₹6 crore overseas, taking the worldwide gross to ₹1,755.50 crore.
Dutch cinemas earned €75,814 from November 19 to 25. The film ranked fifteenth for the week and reached €562,711 in cumulative ticket sales.
Indian cinemas sold an estimated 1.10 million tickets on the day of the offer. That took admissions to 40.33 million in 20 days. Sacnilk’s revised worldwide total through Tuesday is ₹1,738.15 crore.

items.topic: UK and Ireland set an Indian-film record
items.text: Box Office reports that the third weekend took Ramayana past both Dhurandhar: The Revenge and Pathaan in the combined UK and Irish market.
